summary.one_liner: Sphinx is a Python documentation generator that turns reStructuredText sources into HTML, PDF, EPUB, and other formats.
summary.what_it_does: Sphinx uses reStructuredText as its markup language and builds on Docutils for parsing and translation. According to the README, it can output HTML, PDF, plain text, EPUB, TeX, and manual pages. It supports cross-references for functions, classes, and glossary terms, plus a document tree with automatic links between siblings, parents, and children. It generates general and module indices and highlights code with Pygments. HTML output is templated with Jinja 2, and extensions add features such as automatic function documentation and Jupyter notebook support, along with language support for Python, C, C++, JavaScript, and mathematics.
use_cases: Writing project documentation for a Python library
Generating HTML documentation sites from reStructuredText
Producing PDF or EPUB manuals from source files
Documenting APIs with cross-referenced functions and classes
Adding automatic function documentation via extensions
Building documentation that includes Jupyter notebooks
notable: Cross-references for functions, classes, and glossary terms through semantic markup
Extension ecosystem, including autodoc-style function documentation and Jupyter notebook support
Multiple output formats from one reStructuredText source: HTML, PDF, EPUB, TeX, man pages, plain text
caveats: The README does not state platform or dependency limits beyond needing Python and pip
Extensions are needed for many languages and features beyond the core set
